sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: Economic Activities Around Us The root of prosperity is economic activity, the lack of it brings material distress.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: The absence of fruitful economic activity endangers both current prosperity and future growth. — Kauṭilya’s Arthaśhāstra Introduction In Chapter 13, we learnt about two types of activities – economic and non- economic.

sections.content: Activities that create monetary value are called economic activities.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: 196 Exploring Society: India and Beyond Economic Life Around Us Over the decades, the number of economic activities has increased tremendously.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: For example, earlier most people were involved in activities such as agriculture, livestock rearing, production of tools, pottery and weaving cloth.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: As societies progressed, the number of economic activities through which people earn their livelihoods increased vastly.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: Today, there are diverse economic activities such as manufacturing computers, mobile phones and drones; working in banks, schools and hotels; driving various types of vehicles for transportation; making furniture; tailoring clothes using machines; creating software; repairing refrigerators and washing machines; etc.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: Classifying all these activities helps us to understand how they function and the links they have with each other.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: The Classification of Economic Activities into Economic Sectors Some economic activities share similar characteristics and based on this, they can be grouped together or classified into broader groups called economic sectors.
sections.source_evidence: The Classification of Economic Activities into Economic Sectors Some economic activities share similar characteristics and based on this, they can be grouped together or classified into broader groups called economic sectors.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: The three main types of economic sectors are primary, secondary and tertiary economic sectors.
sections.source_evidence: The three main types of economic sectors are primary, secondary and tertiary economic sectors.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: The illustration on the facing page maps out the broad activities under these categories.
sections.source_evidence: The illustration on the facing page maps out the broad activities under these categories.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: Primary activities Those economic activities in which people are directly dependent on nature to produce goods are known as primary activities or primary sector economic activities.
sections.source_evidence: Primary activities Those economic activities in which people are directly dependent on nature to produce goods are known as primary activities or primary sector economic activities.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: Primary sector: The group of activities that involves extraction of raw materials directly from nature such as farming, fishing, forestry, etc.
sections.source_evidence: Primary sector: The group of activities that involves extraction of raw materials directly from nature such as farming, fishing, forestry, etc.

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: Economic Sectors: Broad groups that include various activities that help with the economic prosperity of a nation.
sections.source_evidence: Economic Sectors: Broad groups that include various activities that help with the economic prosperity of a nation.
